You are gentle_otter27, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. const patch="*** Begin Patch

+"""Permission strings used by lla's long listing formatter."""
+
+import stat
+
+
+def file_type(mode: int) -> str:
+    if stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
+        return "dir"
+    if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
+        return "link"
+    if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
+        return "file"
+    if stat.S_ISFIFO(mode):
+        return "fifo"
+    if stat.S_ISSOCK(mode):
+        return "socket"
+    if stat.S_ISCHR(mode):
+        return "char"
+    if stat.S_ISBLK(mode):
+        return "block"
+    return "other"
+
+
+def type_char(mode: int) -> str:
+    return {"dir": "d", "link": "l", "file": "-", "fifo": "p",
+            "socket": "s", "char": "c", "block": "b"}.get(file_type(mode), "?")
+
+
+def format_permissions(mode: int, fmt: str = "symbolic") -> str:
+    """Format an st_mode value using the CLI's permission-format names."""
+    kind = file_type(mode)
+    bits = mode & 0o777
+    octal = f"{bits:03o}"
+    if fmt == "compact":
+        return octal
+    if fmt == "octal":
+        return type_char(mode) + octal
+    if fmt == "binary":
+        return type_char(mode) + f"{bits:09b}"
+    if fmt == "verbose":
+        def triplet(value: int) -> str:
+            return "".join(c if value & bit else "-" for c, bit in (("r", 4), ("w", 2), ("x", 1)))
+        return f"type:{kind} owner:{triplet((bits >> 6) & 7)} group:{triplet((bits >> 3) & 7)} others:{triplet(bits & 7)}"
+    chars = "".join(c if bits & bit else "-" for bit, c in (
+        (0o400, "r"), (0o200, "w"), (0o100, "x"),
+        (0o040, "r"), (0o020, "w"), (0o010, "x"),
+        (0o004, "r"), (0o002, "w"), (0o001, "x")))
+    return type_char(mode) + chars
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r);

+"""Content search rendering for the lla CLI."""
+import csv
+import fnmatch
+import io
+import os
+import re
+
+
+GRAY = "\x1b[38;2;192;197;206m"
+RESET = "\x1b[0m"
+
+
+def find_matches(root, pattern, context=2, case_sensitive=False, show_hidden=True,
+                 file_filter=None):
+    regex = pattern.startswith("regex:")
+    body = pattern[6:] if regex else re.escape(pattern)
+    try:
+        rx = re.compile(body, 0 if case_sensitive else re.IGNORECASE)
+    except re.error:
+        return []
+    found = []
+    def walk(folder):
+        try:
+            entries = sorted(os.scandir(folder), key=lambda e: e.name.casefold())
+        except OSError:
+            return
+        for e in entries:
+            if e.name.startswith(".") and not show_hidden:
+                continue
+            try:
+                if e.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
+                    walk(e.path)
+                elif e.is_file(follow_symlinks=True):
+                    if file_filter and not fnmatch.fnmatch(e.name, "*" + file_filter.lstrip(".")) and not fnmatch.fnmatch(e.name, "*" + file_filter):
+                        continue
+                    try:
+                        data = open(e.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
+                    except OSError:
+                        continue
+                    lines = data.splitlines()
+                    hits = []
+                    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+                        matches = list(rx.finditer(line))
+                        if matches:
+                            hits.append((i, line, matches))
+                    if hits:
+                        found.append((e.path, lines, hits))
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+    if os.path.isfile(root):
+        try:
+            with open(root, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
+                lines=f.read().splitlines()
+            hits=[(i,line,list(rx.finditer(line))) for i,line in enumerate(lines) if rx.search(line)]
+            if hits: found.append((root,lines,hits))
+        except OSError: pass
+    else:
+        walk(root)
+    return found
+
+
+def render_search(root, pattern, context=2, case_sensitive=False, show_hidden=True,
+                  file_filter=None):
+    """Render contextual, line-numbered match output."""
+    files=find_matches(root,pattern,context,case_sensitive,show_hidden,file_filter)
+    out=[]
+    for path, lines, hits in files:
+        out += ["", f"File: {os.path.basename(path)} [{os.path.abspath(path)}]"]
+        for hitidx,(line_no,line,matches) in enumerate(hits):
+            start=max(0,line_no-max(0,context)); end=min(len(lines),line_no+max(0,context)+1)
+            if hitidx and start <= hits[hitidx-1][0]+context:
+                start=max(start,hits[hitidx-1][0]+context+1)
+            for i in range(start,end):
+                colored=GRAY+lines[i]+RESET
+                out.append(f"{i:4} │ {colored}")
+                if i==line_no:
+                    marks=[" "]*len(line)
+                    for m in matches:
+                        for j in range(m.start(),max(m.start()+1,m.end())):
+                            if j<len(marks): marks[j]="^"
+                    out.append(f"{i:4} │ {''.join(marks)}")
+            if hitidx < len(hits)-1: out.append("")
+        out.append("")
+    return "\n".join(out)
+
+
+def search_csv(files):
+    out=io.StringIO(newline="")
+    w=csv.writer(out,lineterminator="\n")
+    w.writerow(["file","line","column","kind","text"])
+    for path,lines,hits in files:
+        for n,line,matches in hits:
+            for m in matches:
+                w.writerow([os.path.abspath(path),n+1,m.start()+1,"match",line])
+    return out.getvalue()

+        for n in sorted(relevant):
+            line=lines[n]; encoded=line.encode("utf-8")
+            text=line+"\n"

+                subs=[]

import os

USAGE:

ARGS:

    <plugin_action>     Action to perform

    -a, --action <action>    Action to perform (alternative to positional)
    -h, --help               Print help information
    -n, --name <name>        Name of the plugin (alternative to positional)
    -r, --args <args>...     Arguments for the plugin action (alternative to positional)
"""


def _plugin_dir():
    # Match the documented default; installed plugins are shared objects.
    cfg = Path.home() / ".config/lla/config.toml"
    try:
        import re
        txt = cfg.read_text()
        m = re.search(r'(?m)^plugins_dir\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)', txt)
        if m:
            return Path(os.path.expanduser(m.group(1)))
    except OSError:
        pass
    return Path.home() / ".config/lla/plugins"


def _libraries():
    """Return loadable ELF candidates and loader diagnostics."""
    found, warnings = [], []
    try:
        entries = _plugin_dir().iterdir()
    except OSError:
        return found, warnings
    for p in entries:
        if not p.is_file() or p.suffix.lower() not in (".so", ".dll", ".dylib"):
            continue
        try:
            magic = p.open("rb").read(4)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if magic == b"\x7fELF":
            found.append(p.stem)
        else:
            warnings.append(f'⚠️ Failed to load plugin library "{p}": {p}: file too short')
    return found, warnings


def run(args):
    """Dispatch plugin subcommands; return True if consumed."""
    if not args or args[0] not in ("plugin", "list-plugins"):
        return False
    cmd, rest = args[0], args[1:]
    if cmd == "list-plugins":
        if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in rest):
            print(LIST_HELP)
        else:
            found, warnings = _libraries()
            for warning in warnings:
                print(warning)
            if not found:
                print("╭─ Plugins ───────────────────────────────────╮")
                print("│   ℹ  No plugins installed.                  │")
                print("│                                             │")
                print("│      Run lla install --help to get started. │")
                print("╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯")
            else:
                print("╭─ Plugins ───────────────────────────────────╮")
                for name in sorted(found):
                    print(f"│   {name}")
                print("╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯")
        return True

    if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in rest):
        print(PLUGIN_HELP)
        return True
    name = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(rest):
        if rest[i] in ("-n", "--name") and i + 1 < len(rest):
            name = rest[i + 1]; i += 2
        elif rest[i] in ("-a", "--action") and i + 1 < len(rest):
            positional.extend((name or "", rest[i + 1])); i += 2
        elif rest[i] in ("-r", "--args"):
            positional.extend(rest[i+1:]); break
        elif rest[i] == "--":
            positional.extend(rest[i+1:]); break
        elif not rest[i].startswith("-"):
            positional.append(rest[i]); i += 1
        else:
            i += 1
    if name:
        positional.insert(0, name)
    plugin = positional[0] if positional else ""
    if not plugin:
        print("""\n✗ Plugin Error

  Plugin name is required.

    lla plugin <name> <action> [args...]
    lla plugin --name <name> --action <action> [--args ...]
  
  Examples:

    lla plugin file_tagger add-tag README.md important
  
  Run 'lla list-plugins' to see available plugins.
""")
    else:
        _, warnings = _libraries()
        for warning in warnings:
            print(warning)
        print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Plugin '%s' not found.\n  \n  No plugins are currently installed. Run 'lla install' to install plugins.\n" % plugin)

"""Read-only metadata view for ZIP and tar archives."""
import os, stat, tarfile, zipfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

def archive_records(filename, recursive=False):
    low=filename.lower()
    if not low.endswith(('.zip','.tar','.tar.gz','.tgz')): return None
    source=os.path.abspath(filename)
    members=[]
    try:
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(filename):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(filename) as z:
                for i in z.infolist():
                    name=i.filename.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
                    isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
                    if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
                    # lla reports ZIP entries without a usable Unix timestamp as epoch.
                    ts='1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'
                    members.append((name,'dir' if isdir else 'file',0 if isdir else i.file_size,mode,ts))
        else:
            with tarfile.open(filename,'r:*') as t:
                for i in t.getmembers():
                    name=i.name.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    typ='dir' if i.isdir() else ('symlink' if i.issym() else ('file' if i.isfile() else 'other'))
                    ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(i.mtime,timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
                    members.append((name,typ,0 if typ=='dir' else i.size,i.mode,ts))
    except (OSError,tarfile.TarError,zipfile.BadZipFile): return None
    known={m[0]:m for m in members}; directories=set()
    for name,*_ in members:
        parts=PurePosixPath(name).parts
        for n in range(1,len(parts)):
            d='/'.join(parts[:n]); directories.add(d)
    for d in directories:
        if d not in known: known[d]=(d,'dir',0,0o755,'1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')
    selected=[]
    for name,item in known.items():
        if recursive or '/' not in name: selected.append(item)
    out=[]
    for name,typ,size,mode,modified in selected:
        basename=name.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        ext=os.path.splitext(basename)[1][1:] or None
        out.append({'path':os.path.basename(filename)+'/'+name,'name':basename,'extension':ext,'file_type':typ,
          'size_bytes':size,'modified':modified,'created':None,'accessed':None,'mode_octal':f'{mode & 0o7777:04o}',
          'owner_user':'root','owner_group':'root','inode':None,'hard_links':None,'symlink_target':None,
          'is_hidden':basename.startswith('.'),'git_status':None,'plugin':({'archive_source':source} if typ=='file' else {})})
    return out

import os, stat, tarfile, zipfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

def archive_records(filename, recursive=False):
    low=filename.lower()
    if not low.endswith(('.zip','.tar','.tar.gz','.tgz')): return None
    source=os.path.abspath(filename)
    members=[]
    try:
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(filename):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(filename) as z:
                for i in z.infolist():
                    name=i.filename.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
                    isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
                    if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
                    # lla reports ZIP entries without a usable Unix timestamp as epoch.
                    ts='1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'
                    members.append((name,'dir' if isdir else 'file',0 if isdir else i.file_size,mode,ts))
        else:
            with tarfile.open(filename,'r:*') as t:
                for i in t.getmembers():
                    name=i.name.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    typ='dir' if i.isdir() else ('symlink' if i.issym() else ('file' if i.isfile() else 'other'))
                    ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(i.mtime,timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
                    members.append((name,typ,0 if typ=='dir' else i.size,i.mode,ts))
    except (OSError,tarfile.TarError,zipfile.BadZipFile): return None
    known={m[0]:m for m in members}; explicit_names=set(known); directories=set()
    for name,*_ in members:
        parts=PurePosixPath(name).parts
        for n in range(1,len(parts)):
            d='/'.join(parts[:n]); directories.add(d)
    for d in directories:
        if d not in known: known[d]=(d,'dir',0,0o755,'1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')
    selected=[]
    for name,item in known.items():
        if recursive or '/' not in name: selected.append(item)
    out=[]
    for name,typ,size,mode,modified in selected:
        basename=name.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        ext=os.path.splitext(basename)[1][1:] or None
        out.append({'path':os.path.basename(filename)+'/'+name,'name':basename,'extension':ext,'file_type':typ,
          'size_bytes':size,'modified':modified,'created':None,'accessed':None,'mode_octal':f'{mode & 0o7777:04o}',
          'owner_user':'root','owner_group':'root','inode':None,'hard_links':None,'symlink_target':None,
          'is_hidden':basename.startswith('.'),'git_status':None,'plugin':({'archive_source':source} if name in explicit_names else {})})
    return out

## Task and constraints

Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` (`lla 0.5.7`) in Python 3.10 under `/workspace`, using only bundled docs and reference CLI behavior. Do not use external sources, wrap the reference executable, or run `compile.sh`. The implementation is collaborative; only code pushed to shared `team/main` is graded. Continue reviewing and pushing fixes until time runs out.

## Progress

A broad CLI implementation and many helper modules are already on shared `main`. My contributions pushed to `main` include:

- `permissions.py`: permission format helper.
- `search_utils.py` and `main.py`: contextual search, CSV search output, JSONL search events, search path behavior, hidden-file handling, and `--search-pipe` dispatch.
- `archive_utils.py` and `main.py`: TAR owner/group and symlink metadata, ZIP/TAR long-view differences, and recursive archive section output.

Recent checks: `python3 -m py_compile main.py search_utils.py archive_utils.py` passed. JSON listing, octal long output, archive ZIP/TAR listing, and tree output matched observed reference fixtures in recent probes.

The latest fetched/merged shared commit seen was `59ae523`; check `git fetch team && git merge team/main` before editing because teammates are actively pushing.

## Immediate next step

A just-run comparison found a concrete recursive-filter mismatch:

```sh
python3 main.py -R --files-only /tmp/lla-fixture
/opt/reference/executable -R --files-only --no-color /tmp/lla-fixture
```

Reference includes a `/tmp/lla-fixture/sub` section containing `z.txt`. Our output omitted that section because the filtered rows no longer include the parent directory, and recursive rendering discovers children through those rows. Fix recursive traversal so it can descend through directories excluded from display filters, while only printing entries that pass filters. Recheck this case and push the fix.

Other cases from that same probe matched:

- `--json /tmp/lla-fixture` metadata and order matched.
- `--permission-format octal -l` matched.
- `-t --no-dotfiles` matched.

## Important implementation/context notes

- User explicitly steered the work back toward continued tool use and whole-program review; do not stop after a status update.
- Use concise commentary updates while working.
- The reference is for observation only. Workspace fixture files are under `/tmp`; query it via normal CLI.
- Search JSON output is ripgrep-style JSONL (`begin`, `match`, `context`, `end`, `summary`), not entry metadata JSON. Timings and some `bytes_printed` stats remain imperfect.
- ZIP long output uses `-` dates and regular-file-style permission markers even for virtual directories. TAR preserves member times and uid/gid names.
- Avoid overlapping main-file edits when a teammate is actively integrating a feature; check the feed and latest shared commit before changing code.
- Do not run tests unless asked; the original task explicitly recommends comparing behavior, and prior work used focused reference comparisons and `py_compile`.
I’ll sync with the shared branch, read the new search findings, then verify the recursive filtering issue and make a targeted fix if it’s still present.
